correctness.rationale: Every edge has four neighboring edges, so two colors must split them 2–2. At rungs S_{i-1}+S_i=2 for S_i=T_i+B_i. If S alternates 0 and 2, consecutive top-rail constraints force their common rung first to 1 and then to 0. Thus B_i=1-T_i. Subtracting the top and bottom constraints then gives T_{i+2}=1-T_i, and either rail equation gives R_{i+1}=1-R_i. The top pattern has least period four, so cyclic consistency requires 4|n. When this holds, T_0,T_1,R_0 are three independent bits and recover all indexed assignments, giving exactly eight. For all n≥3 the even Hamiltonian cycle can be alternately colored, with its perfect-matching complement receiving a third color; properness in the cubic graph gives exactly two neighbors of each other color. One color is impossible. In the cube a witness is top 0011, bottom 1100 and rungs 0101; this contradicts the input-degree parity condition literally stated in Kalinowski et al. §3.
residual_risks: The result uses open edge neighborhoods, not a vertex-based majority condition. The general proof, not the reported finite checks, establishes the count.
